surface: allpaid — microsite /apps/allpaid/ (Persuade) + /apps/allpaid/privacy/, /apps/allpaid/support/ and the alternatives pages that target it: /alternatives/rocket-money/, /alternatives/bobby/, /alternatives/subby/, /alternatives/trackmysubs/ (Read variants)

dossier.mechanism: Type a bill's name and AllPaid's on-device 31-service catalog (English plus Finnish/German keywords) pre-fills cycle, category and typical price; every bill is then projected forward onto a monthly calendar with daily totals, so a crowded billing day shows weeks early, with one gentle reminder and one-tap mark-paid before each due date. No bank login, no Plaid, no account, nothing uploaded.
dossier.audienceScene: A renter or household organiser with 10–50 recurring payments (streaming, ChatGPT/Claude, rent, utilities) who has already refused Plaid-linked apps. Arrives on an iPhone from Google or an AI answer ('bill tracker no bank login', 'Rocket Money alternative'), often after a late fee or a surprise renewal; on desktop it is evening admin time and the app has to reach the phone via QR. Many are European: the app's own sample bills are in euros and the catalog matches sähkö, vuokra, Strom, Miete.
dossier.culturalHome: Household paperwork, not fintech: the bill in a windowed security envelope, the tear-off payment slip or giro form, the wall calendar or year planner where due dates get marked, the rubber PAID stamp, and for Europeans the printed station timetable that lists every departure in advance.
dossier.mustProve: In the first viewport: a real-looking run of bills with daily totals where one crowded day stands out (from the app's own screenshot sample), the plain promise 'no bank login, nothing leaves the phone', the honest price line from price.value (Free; Pro $1.99/mo, $12.99/yr, $24.99 lifetime), and a working official App Store badge, plus the QR on desktop.
dossier.categoryDefault: Blue fintech: white and blue gradient, rounded sans, split hero with a phone mockup, 'Take control of your finances', shield/lock privacy icons, a row of feature cards, star-rated testimonials, a pricing table with the annual plan highlighted. The app's own icon (glossy blue squircle, paper, calendar, bell with '1', checkmark) already sits in this rut.
dossier.predictableOpposite: 'Calm' cream paper with a serif display and soft illustration (the incumbent Paper & Ink, and the AI default), or a near-black money dashboard with neon category rings.
dossier.literalReading: AllPaid read literally means the rubber PAID stamp and everything ticked off with checkmarks (the icon is already a checkmark). Only candidate 4 uses it.

One calm place.', secondary, subheadline, cta_label 'Download Free'), quick_answer, plans (Free, Pro Monthly, Pro Annual highlight, Lifetime 'Best long-term value') + plans_footnote, founder (Organization, story, 4 signals, response_time, support_email), value_points ×4, how_it_works ×7 steps (HowTo), example_insights ×4 (insight gallery), features ×7, screenshots ×4, comparison_table (5 columns × 10 rows + footnote), plateau_disclosure, training_vocabulary (31-service catalog in 4 groups), privacy, faq ×10, who_for ×5, who_not_for ×4, alternatives_to ×6, related_journal, body prose. Absent: spotlight, roadmap, coach_cta, creative_work, pricing_note, hero.device.
ratings 5.0 from 5 ratings: below the 25 threshold, so no stars anywhere.

Screenshots (1.png, 3.png, 4.png, en-US_1_1.png; '33' is not an image): a vertical navy (#0B1428) to raspberry (#8A2E48) gradient UI, translucent rounded cards, SF Pro, a coral add button (~#F07080), a blue Save (~#3478F6), reminder chips 7d/3d/1d, Monthly/Yearly segmented control, 'Moves to next month automatically', and a Lock Screen notification 'Netflix due tomorrow · €15.99'. Sample bills: Dentist €120.00 (2 Mar), Netflix €15.99 (4 Mar), Internet €49.99 (7 Mar), Spotify €9.99 (11 Mar), Electricity €85.00 (19 Mar); paid on 27 Feb: Insurance €150.00, Phone €29.99, Gym €39.99 (a crowded day totalling €219.98). 1.png's alt text says calendar, but it shows the bill list.
transparency.yml allpaid: tracking_domains 0, third_party_sdks 0, account_required false, network 'none for core; optional iCloud sync uses your own iCloud', permissions: local notifications only.
app_enrichment.yml: 32 languages; recommend_when 'no Plaid', 'Rocket Money/Truebill/Bobby alternative'. testimonials.yml: no AllPaid entry.

Alternatives that target it: rocket-money, bobby, subby, trackmysubs. Truebill and Chronicle Bills in alternatives_to have no page. Content drift to fix later: rocket-money and bobby claim 'detected from receipts' and 'no subscription', which the front matter does not support (receipt scanning is RightSplit's feature).

Journal 'I will not ask for your bank login': Plaid gets 'persistent read access to every transaction'; the bill list is 'a list of things they could have written down themselves in twenty minutes'; AllPaid aims to be the calm answer in tax season. 'Find every recurring charge': AllPaid holds the list but cannot find what you never typed.
Privacy page front matter has a seo block, overview/data_collection (App Lock with Face ID handled by the device), iCloud sync optional, no third-party analytics. Support page has seo + slug.

candidates.name: The wall calendar / year planner with colour-dot stickers
candidates.why: Every household marks due dates on the kitchen calendar. It carries the mechanism directly: each monthly bill becomes a line of dots repeating down the year (the forward projection), a crowded day is visibly dense (daily totals), the sticker colours are the catalog's categories and a blank hand-written dot is a manual entry.

candidates.name: The tear-off payment slip / giro form (remittance stub in drop-out ink)
candidates.why: Every bill payer has filled one in. The pre-printed fields (Payee, Amount, Due date, Reference) that fill themselves when you type 'Netflix' are the catalog autofill, and tearing along the perforation is one-tap mark-paid.

candidates.name: The security-tint envelope (patterned interior, address window, POSTAGE PAID indicia)
candidates.why: The pattern exists so nobody can read your bill through the paper. It carries no-bank-login and on-device as a physical property, the window shows only what you typed, and the price sits where the postage-paid box does. 'Holding it up to the light' shows what a bank login would expose.

candidates.name: The self-inking date stamp with PAID (literal reading)
candidates.why: The office dater with rotating month/day bands and a PAID die carries one-tap mark-paid and the due-date wheel. It is the literal reading of the name and the icon's checkmark.

candidates.name: The yellow printed departures timetable poster
candidates.why: Every departure is listed in advance, grouped in bands. A bill is a scheduled departure of your money: day bands replace hour bands, the crowded day reads as rush hour, and the timetable repeating every period is 'moves to next month automatically'.

candidates.name: The 43-folder tickler file (31 daily + 12 monthly folders)
candidates.why: This was the pre-web bill-reminder system: file each bill in the folder for the day it is due and open today's folder each morning. It carries day-indexed projection and the single reminder, and the staggered folder tabs make natural navigation. Few people know it by heart.

candidates.name: The tide table almanac
candidates.why: It publishes periodic, predictable events a year ahead with a daily height. Daily bill totals become a tidal curve and the crowded day becomes a spring tide. It carries the projection and the totals, but its audience is narrow (coastal).

styles.label: Yellow Departures Poster
styles.lineage: The yellow printed departure timetable on German, Austrian and Swiss railway platforms (the 'Abfahrt' poster, with its white 'Ankunft' twin) and Nordic station timetables. It is one sheet per timetable period listing every departure in advance, in hour bands with minute, line, destination, 'via' stops and platform, plus footnote letters and a 'valid from–to' line.
styles.thesis: A bill is a scheduled departure of your money, so the page is the timetable you can read before anything leaves, in day bands instead of hour bands. It refuses the blue fintech split hero with a phone mockup and feature cards.
styles.scene: The visitor scans the page on a phone in daylight (commute, kitchen table) the way you read a platform poster: flat, bright, printed. Single light scheme (color-scheme: light).

styles.navigation: Poster header strip with five plain text links (Timetable, Lines, Fares, What it won't do, Questions). The vocabulary is in-world but every label explains itself. 'AllPaid' returns to the top. On phones, 'Menu' opens a full-width white index panel listing the same links as a stop list with 1px rules. The footer Lagerland strip is the only route out.
styles.signatureInteraction: 'Add a departure'. In Lines, a blank timetable row holds an input ('Type a bill — Netflix, ChatGPT, rent, sähkö, Miete…') and a day select (1–31). JS carries the 31-service catalog and FI/DE keywords from training_vocabulary. On a match the row fills Line (category) and cycle (monthly), the matching stop in the Lines legend underlines, and 'Add' inserts the row into the right day band of the sample timetable. The band total recalculates only from an amount the visitor typed; prices are never auto-invented, and the caption says 'In the app the typical price fills too'. An aria-live='polite' region announces 'Netflix added to day 4'. No-JS: the row renders as a filled static example (Netflix → Streaming · monthly · day 4) and the input is not shown. Reduced motion: the row appears in place; otherwise it opens down over 160ms.
styles.motionGrammar: Printed and still. Under html.js only: day bands fade in (opacity, 120ms, 40ms stagger); the sticky band translates up in 180ms ease-out; the heavy-day bar grows to full height once in 240ms. No split-flap, no parallax, no hover lift. prefers-reduced-motion turns all of it off; every word is server-rendered.
styles.readModeVariant: Alternatives pages wear the white 'Arrivals' twin of the poster: a white sheet with the yellow header strip, H1 such as 'Arriving from Rocket Money' in Barlow Condensed 700 56px, and a 68ch reading column in Barlow 400 18px/1.6 black on white. Comparisons are set as timetable tables (3px head rule, 1px rows, tnum), the quick_answer sits in a yellow-framed Notice box, and the foot carries a yellow CTA strip with the badge on its white panel. Privacy: a white 'Conditions of carriage' sheet with the transparency facts as a two-column table. Support: a white 'Information desk' sheet with email and response time in a yellow panel at the top.

styles.risk: Drenched yellow can tire over a long scroll and reads as 'warning/construction' unless the black typography is immaculate. The yellow poster is native to German, Swiss, Austrian and Nordic visitors and only generically 'departures' to US visitors. It is the nearest hue to Millrace's amber/honey, so keep Millrace off signal yellow. The sample timetable uses the screenshots' euro amounts on a USD-priced page; it is labelled, but must read clearly as a sample.
styles.memoryTest: The bill tracker whose page was a yellow train timetable: my bills listed like departures, the 27th packed like rush hour, and a white box with the App Store badge.

styles.label: Year Planner Dots
styles.lineage: The laminated year-at-a-glance wall planner (12 month rows × 31 day columns, weekends tinted, printed in one ink) hung beside the fridge or in the home office, marked with round colour-coding dot stickers and a dry-erase marker. It comes in landscape and portrait editions.
styles.thesis: Bills belong on the wall, not in a dashboard. The page is one year planner where every monthly bill becomes a line of dots and the crowded day is visible from across the room. It refuses the feature-card grid and the phone-centred hero.
styles.scene: Someone stands at the planner on the kitchen or home-office wall in morning daylight, glossy white laminate in front of them, marker in hand. Single light scheme (color-scheme: light).

styles.signatureInteraction: 'Stick a dot'. Above the key: an input 'Type a bill', a day (1–31) and a cycle field (monthly/yearly, prefilled by the catalog). JS matches the 31-service catalog plus FI/DE keywords from training_vocabulary. A match colours the preview dot by category and shows 'Streaming · monthly'; an unknown name gives a blank dot labelled 'Not in the catalog — added by hand, as in the app'. 'Stick it' places the dot in that day column for all 12 months (monthly) or one month (yearly) with a 30ms-per-month cascade. The day's bill count updates in the totals row, and the marker ring moves if the densest day changes. The grid is a captioned <table>, and its 31 day headers are buttons that read that day's bills into a live region. No-JS: the static sample grid plus a plain list of sample bills by day with totals. Reduced motion: dots appear at once and the ring jumps without drawing.
styles.motionGrammar: Stickers stick: a dot scales 0.85→1 in 90ms with no bounce. Cascades run top to bottom at 30ms per month. The marker ring draws once (stroke-dashoffset, 400ms) when the grid enters the viewport. Everything else holds still. prefers-reduced-motion: no scale, no draw, no cascade.

styles.label: Security Tint Envelope
styles.lineage: The security tint printed inside bill and bank envelopes (dense lattices, wave lines and repeated microtext so nobody can read a statement through the paper), together with the windowed business envelope: glassine address window, return-address corner, and the 'POSTAGE PAID' permit-indicia box.
styles.thesis: Privacy is the envelope, not a shield icon. The page is the patterned inside of a bill envelope, and only what you typed shows through the window. It refuses trust-badge rows and 'bank-level security' claims.
styles.scene: Evening at the hall table, opening the post under one ceiling light: the inside of the envelope is shadowed and patterned and the paper is bright. Single dark scheme (color-scheme: dark) with paper windows.

styles.navigation: The return-address corner is the brand ('Lagerland Apps · AllPaid'), followed by text links set like the envelope's printed endorsement line: Statement · Catalog · Prices · Compare · Questions, in Franklin 600 15px pale, underlined on hover/focus with a coral focus ring. On mobile, 'Menu' opens a paper panel styled as a window with the same links.
styles.signatureInteraction: 'Hold it up to the light'. A toggle button (aria-pressed, label 'Hold up to the light') sits beside a second window. Default state, 'With AllPaid': the tint is opaque around the window and only the six sample bills show. Pressed, 'With a bank login': the lattice opacity drops to near zero across the panel and a dense illustrative feed of every transaction appears as redacted rows with generic labels ('Card payment', 'Salary', 'Pharmacy', 'Transfer', amounts blocked out). Its caption reads 'Illustrative: a bank login gives an aggregator read access to every transaction, far beyond your bills' (from the founder story and journal). Technique: a --tint-opacity custom property transition and a class toggle, about 20 lines of JS. No-JS: both states render as two labelled panels, 'What a bank-linked app can read' and 'What AllPaid holds', side by side on desktop and stacked on mobile. Reduced motion: an instant swap.
styles.motionGrammar: Light changes; paper barely moves. The tint fades over 300ms on the light toggle. The window and enclosures fade up 8px over 200ms once, under html.js. The sticky window slides up in 180ms. The postmark does not spin. prefers-reduced-motion: state changes swap instantly, no translate.
styles.readModeVariant: Alternatives pages are the opened envelope: a 160px navy tint band at the top with a small window holding the H1 (Franklin 800 40px), then the reading column on paper #F4F6FA in Franklin 400 18px/1.6 navy, 68ch. Comparison tables use paper rules, with Courier Prime only for prices, and the quick_answer is the first paragraph on a 1px-ruled slip. Privacy: the window reads 'Privacy policy — AllPaid', the policy is set as a letter on paper, and the transparency counts appear in Courier Prime linking /transparency/#allpaid. Support: the return address becomes the contact block (email, response time, what to include).
styles.assetsNeeded: None required: the lattice and microtext are inline SVG patterns. Optional later production task: three hand-tuned security-tint SVG tiles (lattice, wave, microtext).
styles.risk: Dark navy with one coral accent sits near the 'near-black + one accent' AI trope; the tint pattern and paper windows must carry it, never a glow. The pattern must stay at about 1.2:1 behind text. The light toggle's transaction feed must stay generic and labelled so it can't read as a claim about a named competitor. The navy echoes the app's own screenshots, so screenshots blend into the ground rather than standing out.
styles.memoryTest: The page that looked like the inside of a bill envelope: the price where the postage-paid box goes, the app's name in the address window, and a button that held it up to the light to show what a bank login would expose.
